analysis:
Units 80 and 81 are test-only changes: scripts/test-provider-release-pipeline.py and scripts/test-provider-release-publication.py. They add no runtime provider or coordinator code, so no threat-model control is weakened directly.

I also read the replayed workflow patch in .github/workflows/release-provider.yml. It adds a cluster-runtime facts step that runs after signing, notarization and the final tar hash check. The step deletes the signing keychain and proves the identity is gone before any release code runs. It reads no secrets, unsets r2_public_url and coordinator_url, and runs the app CLI under `env -i`. Sending the block needs publish == 'true' and the per-environment CLUSTER_RUNTIME_SEND variable. The off path is byte-identical to before. Failures only warn unless the block is sent, in which case they fail before registration. The upload-artifact action is pinned by SHA. This matches what the tests assert, and I saw no secret exposure. The facts are produced by the signed app, not by the release key.

The tests cover strict cluster_runtime schema validation, canonical JSON, duplicate-key rejection, the 128-byte derived-ID limit, the 64 KiB registration body cap, and unchanged payload bytes without the block. They also check that only `prepare` accepts --cluster-runtime and that unknown environments are still refused. All of this supports T-054, T-053 and A-017 and does not change authorization.

Open questions for later passes, because the files are outside the supplied scope:
- Whether the production scripts (provider-release-publication.py, provider-cluster-runtime-facts.sh, provider-cluster-runtime-models.py) enforce what the tests assert.
- Whether the coordinator treats cluster_runtime as untrusted advisory data rather than serving authorization.
- Whether the replayed workflow's unseen remainder keeps secrets out of the facts step.

No qualifying finding was identified in the supplied units.
